settings.heading: Details
settings.content:
Built for sensitive teeth and gums. No SLS — a known canker-sore trigger. No harsh scrubbing grit, which is harder than your teeth and wears them down over years.

What is in it. Cold-pressed coconut oil, baking soda, and wildcrafted myrrh. That is the short version.

Food-grade or food-derived. Every ingredient. Safe for incidental swallowing; supervise young kids until they can spit reliably.

Honest trade-off. Closer to a gel than paste. Doesn't foam. Mint is essential-oil mild, not synthetic-amplified.

settings.heading: Ingredients
settings.content:
Purified spring water, organic virgin coconut oil, baking soda (aluminum-free sodium bicarbonate), xanthan gum, wildcrafted myrrh powder, organic stevia.

Variation essential oils:

  • Fresh Mint: organic peppermint, organic spearmint
  • All Natural: organic peppermint, organic spearmint, organic cinnamon, organic clove
  • Cinnamon Spice: organic cinnamon, organic clove

settings.heading: How to Use
settings.content: Use it on a dry brush — do not add water. Shake the bottle first: coconut oil firms below 76°F, so the gel can settle. Squeeze a pea-sized amount onto a dry toothbrush and brush as you normally would for two minutes. There is no SLS in this formula, so it does not need water to work — wetting the brush only thins the gel and it slides off the bristles. It won't foam, and the mint will feel quieter than industrial paste — that's the formula working.

settings.heading: Built around what protects — not what foams.

settings.text: Toothpaste shouldn't trigger the gums it's meant to protect. We built this around what cleans, soothes, and protects — not what foams the most.

settings.title: Organic Virgin Coconut Oil
settings.text: The base. Cold-pressed virgin coconut oil, unrefined, so it keeps everything a lab would take out. Refined oil is cheaper to work with because it is neutral and always the same. Getting it that way strips out most of what makes the oil worth using, so we pay for the unrefined kind.

settings.title: Baking Soda
settings.text: A gentle polish. Aluminum-free baking soda lifts surface stains, and it is softer than your teeth. The cheap grit most brands use is harder than your teeth and wears them down over years of daily brushing. Baking soda does not.

settings.title: Wildcrafted Myrrh
settings.text: A traditional resin. Wildcrafted myrrh has been used in oral care for thousands of years. Most natural toothpastes leave it out, because sourcing it sustainably is expensive and hard to do at scale. We think it earns its place.

During my own healthy-ingredients journey, I flipped over the box of my toothpaste and saw the warning: do not swallow. Why was I putting something in my mouth that wasn't safe to swallow?

From that moment, our family set out to make an effective toothpaste without fluoride — or anything else that would be harmful to swallow. Every ingredient in this tube is food-grade or food-derived. That's not marketing copy. That's the line we drew, and we won't cross it for profit.

— Sean Fillmore

settings.heading: Why doesn't this toothpaste foam?
settings.row_content: Foam comes from synthetic detergents like SLS, which is also a known canker-sore trigger for people prone to them. We left it out. Foaming isn't cleaning — it's a sensory cue you've been trained to expect. Your brush does the cleaning, and the lauric acid, baking soda, and myrrh do the protecting. After a week or two, most customers stop missing the foam.

settings.heading: Why is the texture sometimes firmer or thinner?
settings.row_content: It is a gel, not a paste — thinner than drugstore toothpaste is correct, not a defect. Use it on a dry brush and it stays put; add water and it will run off, because there is no SLS in it to hold it together. Beyond that, the texture shifts batch to batch because cold-pressed virgin coconut oil shifts batch to batch. Every harvest is a little different. Refined oil is uniform because the lab strips that variation out, along with most of what makes the oil worth using. We accept that, because it is what real oil does. Shake before use; coconut oil firms up below 76°F.

settings.heading: Does this toothpaste contain fluoride?
settings.row_content: No fluoride. We made this for people who prefer to avoid it. The cleaning comes from three things: cold-pressed coconut oil, aluminum-free baking soda and wildcrafted myrrh. If you want fluoride too, you can pair this with a fluoride rinse.

settings.heading: Is it safe to swallow? Safe for kids?
settings.row_content:
Every ingredient is food-grade or food-derived: organic virgin coconut oil, aluminum-free baking soda, xanthan gum, wildcrafted myrrh, organic stevia, organic essential oils, purified spring water. With no fluoride in the tube, accidental swallowing isn't the same concern it is with conventional paste. No SLS detergent, no synthetic sweeteners, no artificial flavors.

That said, essential oils are concentrated. We still recommend rinsing and spitting like any toothpaste, and supervising young kids until they can spit reliably. If your child is in the toddler-first-toothpaste stage, ask your pediatric dentist about fluoride needs based on your local water and your child's risk profile.

settings.heading: Is this safe for sensitive teeth and gums?
settings.row_content: Yes — it's what we built it for. No SLS (a known canker-sore trigger). No harsh scrubbing grit (harder than your teeth; wears them down over years). No synthetic flavor amplifiers. Baking soda is softer than your teeth. The myrrh is there because it has been part of oral care for a very long time. People with sensitive mouths are who we made this for.

settings.heading: Why is the mint flavor so mild?
settings.row_content: The mint here is essential-oil mild — organic peppermint and spearmint, not synthetic flavor amplifiers. If you're used to industrial toothpaste, the first few brushings will feel quiet. Many customers come to prefer it. The Cinnamon Spice variation is more assertive if you want a stronger hit, because cinnamon essential oil is naturally stronger than mint.

settings.heading: How is this different from other natural toothpastes?
settings.row_content:
"Natural" is essentially unregulated, and a lot of it isn't very. Read any natural toothpaste's ingredient list against ours and you'll typically find one or more of:

  • A foaming agent — SLS, sodium lauroyl sarcosinate, or sodium cocoyl glutamate. We use none. Foam doesn't clean, and SLS is a known canker-sore trigger.
  • An abrasive harder than enamel — hydrated silica, calcium carbonate, or charcoal. We use baking soda, which is softer than enamel and adds pH balancing.
  • A tooth-coating thickener — glycerin or sorbitol. We use xanthan gum, which gives the paste structure without coating teeth.
  • Titanium dioxide for the bright-white look. We leave the paste the color of its actual ingredients.
  • Hydroxyapatite as a marketing-friendly remineralizer. We rely on baking soda neutralizing oral acid and saliva doing what saliva does.

Our list is shorter and we name what's missing as plainly as what's present. The wildcrafted myrrh in particular — most natural brands skip it because consistent sourcing is hard to scale.

settings.row_content: Use it on a dry brush — do not add water. Shake the bottle first: coconut oil firms up below 76°F, so the gel can settle. Squeeze a pea-sized amount onto a dry toothbrush and brush as you normally would for two minutes. There is no SLS in this formula, so it does not need water to work — wetting the brush only thins the gel and it runs off. It won't foam. The mint will feel quieter than industrial paste. Many customers report teeth feel polished after use — a side effect of the lauric acid plus baking soda doing their work.
